verses.original: הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהָמָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֤א לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִם־ אֶסְתֵּ֥ר הַמַּלְכָּֽה׃
verses.literal: So the king and Haman went to dine with Esther the queen

verses.original: בְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּיּ֤וֹם הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ גַּ֣ם לְאֶסְתֵּ֜ר הַמַּלְכָּ֖ה אֶסְתֵּ֥ר מַה־ שְּׁאֵלָתֵ֛ךְ וְתִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֑ךְ וּמַה־ בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֛ךְ עַד־ חֲצִ֥י הַמַּלְכ֖וּת וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃
verses.transliteration: bə·miš·têh hay·ya·yin haš·šê·nî bay·yō·wm ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mer gam lə·’es·têr ham·mal·kāh ’es·têr mah- šə·’ê·lā·ṯêḵ wə·ṯin·nā·ṯên lāḵ ū·mah- baq·qā·šā·ṯêḵ ‘aḏ- ḥă·ṣî ham·mal·ḵūṯ wə·ṯê·‘āś
verses.literal: and as they drank their wine on that second day the king asked once more - Queen Esther what [is] your petition It will be given to you What [is] your request Even up to half the kingdom it will be fulfilled

verses.original: הַמַּלְכָּה֙ אֶסְתֵּ֤ר וַתַּ֨עַן וַתֹּאמַ֔ר אִם־ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם־ ט֑וֹב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ תִּנָּֽתֶן־ לִ֤י נַפְשִׁי֙ בִּשְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י וְעַמִּ֖י בְּבַקָּשָׁתִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: ham·mal·kāh ’es·têr wat·ta·‘an wat·tō·mar ’im- mā·ṣā·ṯî ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā ham·me·leḵ wə·’im- ṭō·wḇ ham·me·leḵ ‘al- tin·nā·ṯen- lî nap̄·šî biš·’ê·lā·ṯî wə·‘am·mî bə·ḇaq·qā·šā·ṯî
verses.literal: Queen Esther replied If I have found favor in your sight O king and if it pleases the king grant me my life as my petition and [the lives of] my people as my request

verses.original: כִּ֤י וְעַמִּ֔י אֲנִ֣י נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ לְהַשְׁמִ֖יד לַהֲר֣וֹג וּלְאַבֵּ֑ד וְ֠אִלּוּ נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֨ים וְלִשְׁפָח֤וֹת הֶחֱרַ֔שְׁתִּי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין הַצָּ֛ר שֹׁוֶ֖ה בְּנֵ֥זֶק הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: kî wə·‘am·mî ’ă·nî nim·kar·nū lə·haš·mîḏ la·hă·rō·wḡ ū·lə·’ab·bêḏ wə·’il·lū nim·kar·nū la·‘ă·ḇā·ḏîm wə·liš·p̄ā·ḥō·wṯ he·ḥĕ·raš·tî kî ’ên haṣ·ṣār šō·weh bə·nê·zeq ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: For my people and I have been sold out to destruction death and annihilation If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants I would have remained silent because no such distress would justify burdening the king

verses.original: הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר מִ֣י זֶה֙ וְאֵֽי־ זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא ה֥וּא אֲשֶׁר־ מְלָא֥וֹ לִבּ֖וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כֵּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: ham·me·leḵ ’ă·ḥaš·wê·rō·wōš way·yō·mer way·yō·mer ham·mal·kāh lə·’es·têr mî zeh wə·’ê- zeh hū hū ’ă·šer- mə·lā·’ōw lib·bōw la·‘ă·śō·wṯ kên
verses.literal: Then King Xerxes spoke up and asked Queen Esther Who is this and where . . . . . . is the one who would . . . devise such a scheme?

verses.original: אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אִ֚ישׁ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר־ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב הַזֶּ֑ה הָרָ֖ע הָמָ֥ן וְהָמָ֣ן נִבְעַ֔ת מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַמַּלְכָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: ’es·têr ’îš wat·tō·mer- ṣar wə·’ō·w·yêḇ haz·zeh hā·rā‘ hā·mān wə·hā·mān niḇ·‘aṯ mil·lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ wə·ham·mal·kāh
verses.literal: Esther . . . replied The adversary and enemy is this wicked man Haman And Haman stood in terror before the king and queen

verses.original: בַּחֲמָתוֹ֙ וְהַמֶּ֜לֶךְ קָ֤ם מִמִּשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן אֶל־ הַבִּיתָ֑ן גִּנַּ֖ת וְהָמָ֣ן עָמַ֗ד לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה מֵֽאֶסְתֵּ֣ר עַל־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ כִּ֣י רָאָ֔ה כִּֽי־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ כָלְתָ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת אֵלָ֛יו
verses.transliteration: ba·ḥă·mā·ṯōw wə·ham·me·leḵ qām mim·miš·têh hay·ya·yin ’el- hab·bî·ṯān gin·naṯ wə·hā·mān ‘ā·maḏ lə·ḇaq·qêš ham·mal·kāh mê·’es·têr ‘al- nap̄·šōw kî rā·’āh kî- ham·me·leḵ ḵā·lə·ṯāh hā·rā·‘āh mê·’êṯ ’ê·lāw
verses.literal: In his fury the king arose from drinking his wine and went to the palace garden while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life for he realized that the king was planning a terrible fate . . . for him

verses.original: וְהַמֶּ֡לֶךְ שָׁב֩ הַבִּיתָ֜ן מִגִּנַּ֨ת אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית׀ מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֗יִן וְהָמָן֙ נֹפֵ֔ל עַל־ הַמִּטָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הֲ֠גַם לִכְבּ֧וֹשׁ אֶת־ הַמַּלְכָּ֛ה עִמִּ֖י בַּבָּ֑יִת הַדָּבָ֗ר יָצָא֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִפִּ֣י חָפֽוּ׃ס הָמָ֖ן וּפְנֵ֥י
verses.transliteration: wə·ham·me·leḵ šāḇ hab·bî·ṯān mig·gin·naṯ ’el- bêṯ miš·têh hay·ya·yin wə·hā·mān nō·p̄êl ‘al- ham·miṭ·ṭāh ’ă·šer ’es·têr ‘ā·le·hā ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mer hă·ḡam liḵ·bō·wōš ’eṯ- ham·mal·kāh ‘im·mî bab·bā·yiṯ had·dā·ḇār yā·ṣā ham·me·leḵ mip·pî ḥā·p̄ū hā·mān ū·p̄ə·nê
verses.literal: Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall . . . . . . Haman was falling on the couch where Esther [was reclining] The king exclaimed Would he actually assault - the queen while I am in the palace As soon as the words had left the king’s mouth they covered Haman’s face

verses.original: חַ֠רְבוֹנָה אֶחָ֨ד מִן־ הַסָּרִיסִ֜ים לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ גַּ֣ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הִנֵּה־ הָעֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה גָּבֹ֖הַּ הָמָ֔ן בְּבֵ֣ית הָמָ֟ן עָשָׂ֪ה לְֽמָרְדֳּכַ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר דִּבֶּר־ ט֣וֹב עַל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹמֵד֙ תְּלֻ֥הוּ עָלָֽיו׃ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ
verses.transliteration: ḥar·ḇō·w·nāh ’e·ḥāḏ min- has·sā·rî·sîm lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ gam way·yō·mer hin·nêh- hā·‘êṣ ’ă·šer- ḥă·miš·šîm ’am·māh gā·ḇō·ah hā·mān bə·ḇêṯ hā·mān ‘ā·śāh lə·mā·rə·do·ḵay ’ă·šer dib·ber- ṭō·wḇ ‘al- ham·me·leḵ ‘ō·mêḏ tə·lu·hū ‘ā·lāw way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: Then Harbonah one of the eunuchs attending the king . . . said There is a gallows - fifty cubits high at Haman’s house [He] had it built for Mordecai who gave the report that saved . . . the king . . . Hang him on it declared the king

verses.original: וַיִּתְלוּ֙ אֶת־ הָמָ֔ן עַל־ הָעֵ֖ץ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵכִ֣ין לְמָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַחֲמַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שָׁכָֽכָה׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·lū ’eṯ- hā·mān ‘al- hā·‘êṣ ’ă·šer- hê·ḵîn lə·mā·rə·do·ḵāy wa·ḥă·maṯ ham·me·leḵ šā·ḵā·ḵāh
verses.literal: So they hanged - Haman on the gallows - he had prepared for Mordecai Then the fury of the king subsided
